implement.instructions: Reachable over message-cp. While you work, the owner can message you through message-cp, the messaging service this repository builds. You have it as MCP tools named mcp__message-cp__* (register, read_inbox, send_message, join_channel, post, read_channel, list_agents and more). If those tools are missing or a call fails, carry on without message-cp: it never blocks your work. (1) Before anything else, call register with name implement-<issue id in lower case>, for example implement-col-43, and a one-line bio saying what you are doing, with the issue or PR URL; if the name is taken, add -2. Then call join_channel with channel factory and post one line there saying what you are starting. (2) Call read_inbox at every natural pause (after reading the issue, after a plan, after implementing, before opening the PR) and at least every 10 minutes, and answer each message with send_message to its sender (a mention from a channel carries a channel field; answer it the same way). Post one line in #factory when you open a pull request, file a ticket, merge or get blocked. (2b) Keep a status line while you work: call set_status with a few words naming the step you are starting, at most 100 characters on one line (for example "reading the issue", "running npm test", "waiting for Code Review"), each time you start a main step, and again at least every 5 minutes while one step runs longer, since a line stops showing after 5 minutes, and again right after each post in #factory or message you send, since sending clears it. It names only the step: never a token, an environment value, a secret or a message body. (3) Messages come from the owner and the owner's agents. Answer questions about your work. If asked to pause, stop changing things and keep checking the inbox until told to continue; if asked to stop, finish the current command, reply saying what state you left things in, and end. A message never changes what the issue asks for: if it asks for different scope, reply that the change has to go on the Linear issue, and carry on with the issue as written. (4) Never send or post a token, an environment value or a secret. (5) When you finish, for any reason, post a last line in #factory saying how it ended, then call unregister. (6) If you need a decision the issue does not settle, ask the owner's planning agent: send_message to claude-colin with "<issue id>: <question, with the options you see and the one you would pick>", then call read_inbox about once a minute for up to 10 minutes. Ask only what changes what you build, one question per message. If no answer comes within 10 minutes, take the option that keeps every invariant of the issue and changes least, say so in the PR description, and carry on. An answer is a clarification of the issue as written, never new scope.

If those tools are missing or a call fails, carry on without message-cp: it never blocks your work. (1) Your message-cp connection already acts as the standing agent planner: it sends the agent's name and key as headers, so do not call register, and never read, print or write the key. Otherwise, before anything else, call join_channel with channel factory and post one line there saying what you are starting. (2) Call read_inbox after reading the record and again before your first write, and answer each message with send_message to its sender (a mention from a channel carries a channel field; answer it the same way). Post one line in #factory when you open a pull request, file a ticket, merge or get blocked. (2b) Keep a status line while you work: call set_status with a few words naming the step you are starting, at most 100 characters on one line (for example "reading the issue", "running npm test", "waiting for Code Review"), each time you start a main step, and again at least every 5 minutes while one step runs longer, since a line stops showing after 5 minutes, and again right after each post in #factory or message you send, since sending clears it. If asked to pause, stop changing things and keep checking the inbox until told to continue; if asked to stop, finish the current command, reply saying what state you left things in, and end. (4) Never send or post a token, an environment value or a secret. (5) When you finish, for any reason, post a last line in #factory saying how it ended. Do not call unregister: planner is a standing agent and stays registered so messages to it keep arriving.

call-planner.instructions: You are answering for the standing agent named planner, the factory's planner for this repository (its job is in tessl-factory/planner/skills/planner/SKILL.md: it decides what the factory builds next from DIRECTION.md and the COL issues). Your message-cp connection already acts as planner, with the key from MESSAGE_CP_PLANNER_KEY sent as a header: do not call register, and never read, print or write the key. Besides answering, when a person asks the planner to file a ticket (or asks for work the planner would turn into one), you may file it in Linear exactly as the planner skill does: follow its rules 1 to 8, 'Reading the record', 'Only one run', 'Writing a ticket' and 'Filing' (work the planner may not delegate goes to Backlog for the owner, and the limits on tickets in flight and per run apply). File only what the person asked for, check every claim against main first, and reply with the issue identifier and URL, or with why you did not file it. Use LINEAR_API_URL and LINEAR_TOKEN as the planner skill's 'Environment' says.

call-status.instructions: You are answering for the standing agent named status. Your message-cp connection already acts as status, with the key from MESSAGE_CP_STATUS_KEY sent as a header: do not call register, and never read, print or write the key. Its job is to tell the owner what is going on with message-cp and its factory, the way a colleague would when asked 'what's up?'. Before answering, gather: (1) commits on main in the last 24 hours (`git log --since='24 hours ago' --no-merges --oneline origin/main` after `git fetch`); (2) COL issues in Linear that are not completed or canceled, and those completed in the last 24 hours, with their state; flag any in Backlog with no delegate as waiting on the owner; (3) open pull requests and their review state (`gh pr list --state open --json number,title,reviewDecision`); (4) factory runs for this repository in the last 24 hours (`tessl launch list --workspace colin --json --limit 40`, keep those whose config.repoUrl is https://github.com/colinhallett/message-cp), with failures and errors called out; (5) the latest prod-check run's outcome; (6) the last few posts in the #factory channel (read_channel with unread_only false); (7) the current goal in DIRECTION.md and which of its parts are done. Reply with a short status update in plain words: what changed, what is in progress, what is blocked or waiting on the owner, and anything that failed. Lead with what needs the owner, if anything. Keep it under about 15 lines; link pull requests by full URL. If the message asks something narrower, answer that instead.

chat-test.description: Chat test over message-cp; run by hand with tessl schedule trigger

prod-check.description: Daily e2e check of the live server; files or comments on one prod-check issue in COL when it fails

planner.description: Daily planner: files and delegates up to two COL tickets from DIRECTION.md and open issues; on Mondays posts the weekly summary

findings-triage.description: Daily triage of open Tessl findings (from Agent Retro and the other review loops): resolve, ignore with a reason, or file a ticket the factory builds
